newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-Cemig still a long-term buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Cemig still a long-term buy.

text.p: Robert Fleming & Co Ltd said it has reiterated its long-term buy recommendation on Brazilian state-owned electrical firm Cemig despite a drop in first-quarter earnings.

-- "Looking at Cemig's first-quarter 1997 numbers for an indication of upside potential is like valuing a Ferrari with a Ford engine before the complete overhaul," Fleming analyst Walter Stoeppelwerth said.
-- He said first-quarter results reflected a "lackadaisical cost containment that has disappointed even the most optimistic investors in the last 18 months."

-- But, he added, the strategic plan created by Minas Gerais state's new strategic partner in Cemig, a group led by AES Corp , has likely been approved by the state and will eventually raise the company's value to that of Chile's electrical giants.

-- Cemig this year must asbsorb a seven-percent hike in U.S. dollar tariff for bying power from Itaipu dam, an eight-percent monetary variation and a hike in power-purchasing costs to buy energy from Furnas.
-- But he added: "We still think Cemig looks attractive to its peers."
-- Cemig's preferred was up 2.15 percent at 57.10 reais and its common rose 1.55 percent to 52.30 reais at 1632 local/1532 edt in Sao Paulo.
